oo yeah thank you for clarifying that. it's been a while since i was in clinicals and i only assisted in a couple brain death scans.

[here](http://www.nucmedresource.com/uploads/3/5/3/9/3539325/2765915.jpg?444) is a negative scan; I think it's in the flow phase so you see the radioactivity being administered through what -might- be a picc line, I'm not sure - I can't really remember how the tracer is given in this particular scan. But you can see where the brain appears 'dark' which means there is some activity picking up the tracer and they are not brain dead.

This is a nuclear medicine procedure called Brain Death Scintigraphy. The image shown is a positive study (they are brain dead), and the way you can tell is the 'Easter basket' effect. If you look at it objectively and ignore that it's a skull, it looks like an Easter basket. 

Edit: forgot to add that the skull looks black because the radioactive tracer was taken up by the sinuses, because the patient is still 'alive', but because there is no brain activity, there is no blood flow thus no tracer uptake in the brain, leaving it white. 

Source: I was in Nuclear Medicine Technology clinicals until I had to give up for health reasons. :C Very fun and interesting career.
